title: התאנה שאינה פרי — והצרעה שבתוכה
summary: A young fig (syconium) is an inside-out bouquet of hundreds of flowers behind a scale-lined eye (ostiole); the 1.5–2 mm female fig wasp squeezes in, loses her wings, spreads pollen, lays eggs in short-style flowers (galls) while long-style flowers become seeds, and dies inside (ficin); wingless males open the exit, females leave with pollen and have ~1–2 days to find another tree's receptive figs — within-tree synchrony, between-tree asynchrony (4-tree model); Namib Ficus sycomorus pollen carried 160–164 km by wind (Ahmed et al. 2009); Gilgal figs 11,400 yrs, parthenocarpic, planted from cuttings ~1,000 yrs before wheat (Kislev, Hartmann, Bar-Yosef 2006; disputed); sycamore in Israel lacks its wasp, gashing + ethylene ripens it in 3–4 days, Amos 'בולס שקמים'; Galil & Eisikowitch (TAU); 1,274 vertebrate species eat figs.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (2 rounds) — nits left: ~30 min with the test (word count at the series norm, above the 1,100-word target); step-4 shared text gently hints that trees must differ in timing before the guess
